title: Bound QUERY savings from two paid idles on different binary caller arms
body:
Across all 480 tested pairs, preserving the two body masks forces the identity transport in the named two-register model. The midpoint epsilon correction has rank four; granting two odd heads raises the rank to six.

## Scope and source

Uses the literal compact #7952 caller with all other native actions, idles and terminal masks fixed. A positive price-only nominal pair fails both operators. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-cross-stage-idles-rank/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. Both complete formal and native operators, actual 36/48-call tariffs and 216 basis triples per pair passed the cold replay. The nominal deletion mutation fails 19 forward and 37 adjoint rows. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Allow a larger simultaneous stage or register interface and verify its signed price and full operator.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
